newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - MARCH 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - MARCH 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Casino king Sol Kerzner was granted an urgent intermin interdict in the Umtata High Court to stop Transkei's attorney- general from issuing a warrant for his arrest or extradition on charges of bribery, corruption, fraud and contravention of the Companies Act.

- The government would use a four billion rand improvement in tax collection to fill most of a 6.5 billion rand hole in the new budget and by doing so would achieve its target of a four percent deficit, South African Chamber of Business economist Ben van Rensburg forecast.

- Proposed changes to the draft white paper on motor vehicle insurance - discussed behind closed doors in parliament - would severely limit the benefits paid to iinjured people, an attorney has claimed.
- The South African Broadcasting Corp has accepted recommendations which could save it 450 million rand, but which would result in up to 1,400 job cuts, it said.
- Financial services group Fedsure Holdings Ltd lifted attributable income 40 percent to 133.1 million rand for the year to December, buoyed by strong growth in all business units.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Bearish sentiment overwhelmed the gold market on Monday as weakness in the metal continued following its fall below the psychologically important level of $350 an ounce at the weekend.

- Property stocks have showed a return of more than 20 percent in the first six weeks of this year and have shown further growth since then. This was a clear indication that the sector was undergoing its long-awaited rerating, analysts said.
- A senior executive has suddenly left the Don Group in the wake of efforts to restore operational efficiencies at the executive apartment and restaurant company after a below-par interim showing.

- Genbel , the financial investment group, is considering opening a commodity trading desk when exchange controls are lifted, executive director Peter Cronshaw said. This would bring it back to its roots as a commodity-based exploration company.
- Enviroserv , the listed waste management company, would merge with its leading competitor, Waste-Tech, in a 189 million rand share swap, the two companies said.
SAKE-BEELD
- Hotel and gambling magnate Sol Kerzner's lawyers have made an urgent court application to prevent the attorney-general of the Transkei region seeking his extradition from Britain.
- Fedsure Holdings Ltd increased its attributable income for the year to end-December by 40 percent to 133.1 million rand.
- All worries about the legal status of contracts entered into by the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA) have been settled by draft legislation giving the DBSA formal legal status.
- New, tougher mortgage lending conditions are to be phased in for state officials over the 20 months.
THE STAR

- The South African Broadcasting Corp has accpted recommendations to reduce its staff by 25 percent and to adopt a restructuring programme which promises to save the corporation 450 million rand over the next two years.
- Pressure is mounting on the Truth and Reconciliation Commission to expose apartheid-era police informers, including some who allegedly now occupy top government positions.
- A fire which destroyed much of Pretoria city council's administration complex was caused by a faulty electrical component in a light fitting, not by arson, investigators said.
